story: Kumbhakarna, Ravana's giant brother, asked Brahma for a boon. Saraswati twisted his tongue, so instead of asking for Indra's throne (Indrasana) he asked for endless sleep (Nidrasana). He slept for six months at a time and woke only to eat.
belief: He is remembered as a huge-hearted warrior, loyal to his brother. His name is used in India today, often affectionately, for anyone who sleeps too much.
turns: Woken for the war, he told Ravana plainly that taking Sita was wrong, then fought for him anyway out of loyalty, and was killed by Rama in battle.
facts: His name means 'the one with ears like pots'.
The gods feared his appetite, which is why they tricked him over the boon.
Many retellings treat him as more honourable than Ravana.
